newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia party leader says his supporters afraid.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia party leader says his supporters afraid.

text.p: The head of Indonesia's Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) said a climate of fear in the run-up to next month's elections is preventing some people from openly declaring their support for the PPP.

"This happens because political conditions are not conducive enough to exercise the freedom to choose because people are afraid of the possible consequences of choosing the PPP," Antara news agency on Monday quoted PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum as saying.
Metareum made the comments in an address on Sunday to party supporters at a function in Banjarmasin, capital of South Kalimantan province.
PPP supporters have clashed with those of the ruling Golkar party in recent weeks in a number of cities in central Java. Indonesia holds general elections on May 29.

On Wednesday, at least three government offices, 11 vehicles and dozens of homes were damaged and 14 people injured in the central Java town of Wonosobo in clashes between supporters of the two parties, newspapers said.

Troops were called out in the coastal central Java town of Pekalongan last week after hundreds of apparent PPP supporters attacked a housing estate mostly inhabited by civil servants. Civil servants are mainly Golkar supporters.
Riots broke out in Pekalongan, a PPP stronghold, two weeks ago after reports that a popular folk singer who has campaigned for the PPP in the past would be a Golkar candidate in the elections.
Only three political parties -- the PPP, Golkar and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) -- are allowed to contest Indonesia's general elections.

With Indonesia's tightly controlled electoral system, Golkar is almost assured of achieving a landslide victory. It has set a target of more than 70 percent of the vote, up from around 68 percent at the last poll in 1992.
The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent in 1992.
